change: in-place hot GEMM: hot experts read from their resident row instead of being copied into a k-slot store
method: bench/bench_hotsets_ab.py, REPS=7 interleaved x N_TOK=96, old tree = git archive HEAD, new tree = the change; runs back to back on the same box
headline: +1.9% (p=0.025) at the informed hot set, +0.7% at index, +0.1% (n.s.) at pure streaming. The gain scales with hot-set coverage, which is what it should do: the change removes exactly the re-copy a hot hit used to pay.
the_correction: A byte count motivated this change and OVERSTATED it. On granite the hot re-copy was 48.5% of all gather traffic, which read as a large lever. It is not: that copy runs at HBM bandwidth (~5 us/expert, as pipelined.py's own comment predicted), while the PCIe cold reads are what bind. Removing 37% of gather BYTES bought 1.9% of TIME because they were the cheap bytes. Bytes are not time -- the same lesson the informed-hot-set null taught on granite, in the opposite direction.
regression_found_and_fixed: First measurement showed -0.7% (p=0.013) on the PURE-STREAMING config: with an empty hot set there is nothing to gain, but the new per-fetch row dispatch ran anyway. Guarded on n_hot, after which streaming is +0.1% (p=0.225, i.e. unchanged). The change is now non-negative on every config measured.
why_olmoe_not_gpt_oss: gpt-oss-20b does not fit the A2000 under this engine (it keeps the base resident), and two rented boxes failed to provision. OLMoE is the better test bed anyway: it is the same thin-link card docs/RESIDENCY-ENGINES.md measured, and reads demonstrably BIND on it -- informed hot sets are +24.2% (p=0.002) here, replicating that doc's +19%. granite, by contrast, showed no informed-vs-index effect at all, so it could not have resolved this.
